title: Tests that catch real bugs
hints: Think like a bug: what would a hurried colleague get wrong? Swapping the arguments, averaging per-interval ratios, forgetting the error case, rounding, or ignoring all but the first interval.

Write hand-checked cases that each expose one bug: a single pair (12, 10 → 1.2), two intervals at different loads ([1500, 3600] over [1000, 3000] gives 1.275, not 1.35), a value that isn't a round number (1.234 over 1 gives 1.234), and `with pytest.raises(ValueError): pue(5.0, 0.0)`.

assert pue(12.0, 10.0) == pytest.approx(1.2); assert pue([1500.0, 3600.0], [1000.0, 3000.0]) == pytest.approx(1.275); assert pue(1.234, 1.0) == pytest.approx(1.234); with pytest.raises(ValueError): pue(5.0, 0.0)

misconceptions.float-equality: Comparing floats with == rejects correct code (0.3 / 0.1 is 2.9999999999999996); compare with a tolerance.
